      Reaches

      —

      Filled boxes are entry points — where the outside world comes in. There are 44 of them and they are the reading order: 7 reached from a pointer or wheel event, 3 from a key press, 30 from a control in the interface, 4 components React mounts for a route, and 0 the browser itself calls. Every one was found by reading the source — a call inside a registered listener, inside a JSX handler prop, or inside an effect the interface drives — not by picking the ones that looked important.

      Grey boxes are test-only, and 2 boxes are struck through. 58 functions have no production caller at all; a suite is the only thing that depends on them, which is a real constraint on changing them and worth seeing. The struck-through ones are named nowhere in src/ but at their own definition, tests included: m1eng.setPreBake, m1ewc._checkEraseWatchdogForTests. Each is a candidate for deletion — after a check by hand, since a function reached through a table or a string would read the same way.

      Faint lines stay inside one file; solid ones leave it. That is the distinction worth drawing at this scale. A block whose edges are nearly all faint is self-contained — scaleBar/catalog, clipperOutline — and a block with a spray of solid lines leaving it is where the coupling lives. KobinEngine and the five files mixed onto its prototype are the obvious ones.

      Nothing on this page calls 780 of these functions, and 2 of them are named nowhere else at all. Not the other 778. A call is only drawn when it resolves to a definite target; anything else is dropped rather than guessed at, so no incoming line means not proven, never not there. Click a function with a dashed outline and the panel says which case it is. The breakdown:

      Why there is no lineCountWhat it actually means
      passed as value152Exported, passed as a callback, or held somewhere — named without being called at a site the extractor reads.
      called via an object420Reached as thing.method() on a value whose type is not resolvable from the source. EventLatency.report is one: the hook calls eng.eventLatency.report().
      React component34React renders it as <Component/>. It is never called by name.
      getter110get inScale() and friends are read, not called, so there is no call syntax anywhere to find.
      test only60Nothing in the running app reaches it; a suite does. clipperOutline.clipPolysToRect is one, and its own file header says so.
      language protocol2toJSON. JSON.stringify invokes it by protocol, with the name appearing nowhere.
      no reference at all2A function that appears exactly once in src/, at its own definition. The 2026-08-31 cleanup cleared the list; anything appearing here is new.

      414 of the edges were also read off the source by hand, and the extractor independently finds 390 of those — which is the check on whether it is reading calls correctly rather than plausibly.

      Blocks with a dashed outline are not running, and are hidden until you ask for them. They are 1,117 of the functions here — the retired KobinEngineV0, the cubic-pipeline curvePerimeter, the polyline strokeShape, the scene index by brute force, the rasteriser's coverage, and the rest of src/engine/__oracles__/: independent implementations the shipping code is checked against, reachable only from test suites, so webpack has never bundled any of it. They are on this page because they are in the repository and the promise here is that every function is; they lay out below everything live so that hiding them costs the rest of the graph nothing. The four dev routes that used to sit alongside them were deleted on 2026-08-31.

      Every function in src/ outside the test suites, and every call that can be read off the source. 7,287 of the calls carry a file:line for the call site, so any line here can be checked against the code. Laid out offline — files layered by the calls between them, functions ordered inside each file by its own calls — so the page ships static SVG and no layout library.
